1:א: (1) A place that has three partitions — meaning such as a mavo open on the fourth side, or a courtyard where one of its walls was breached and between them is open to karmelit or reshus ha-rabbim:
1:ב: (2) The Sages forbade moving objects in it — within four amot; and the reason they forbade it is that since the fourth side is fully open it somewhat resembles reshus ha-rabbim, and if we permit this they will come to move objects also in reshus ha-rabbim; and see Biur Halacha:
1:ג: (3) Some correction on the fourth side — meaning as explained below in seif 2 and seif 3, each according to its law:
2:א: (4) That was breached — meaning to a forbidden place for it:
2:ג: (6) Up to ten amot — and "up to" includes it; for although generally we hold that if a wall was breached ten amot the breach is considered an opening, here since the entire wall is missing we cannot consider this place an opening:
2:ד: (7) In one place — meaning at the top of the wall:
2:ה: (8) One tefach from here, etc. — not specifically one tefach but two mashehuyin suffice, as likewise for placing pasin l'chatchila, and as Beit Yosef wrote; and see Biur Halacha:
2:ו: (9) At a height of ten tefachim — and it need not be equal in height to the other walls; however below this it has no name of partition at all:
2:ז: (10) Since it is fully — this "fully" is not precise, for even if two or three tefachim remained from the wall, any minority relative to the breach requires correction; rather it comes to exclude where standing is greater, for there we hold the majority is as the whole and it is as closed, and even though it does not hold four tefachim, any slight amount more than the breach suffices:
2:ח: (11) Until there remains in it less than three — meaning that one corrects the breach in part and only less than three remains, for then it is as lavud; and all the more if the breach was only less than three, for then no correction is needed for this reason:
2:ט: (12) Even if it is not fully — this wording is not precise, for even when standing is greater than the breach it is also forbidden, as if the entire wall were breached. And tzurat hapetach helps even when it is fully:
3:א: (13) They permitted by a lechi — and although in a courtyard we require specifically a pas four tefachim wide, here the Sages were lenient; and the reason is that the more something is made for dwelling and private uses, the more complete partitions are required; therefore courtyards, whose custom is that homeowners use them more for private uses and eating, require their partitions to be more complete so that there is reshut ha-yachid upon them, unlike mavo'ot where they do not use them for private uses; therefore a mavo suffices with a lechi; and see below siman 366 that this is specifically when its opening is not wider than ten amot, and further details see there:
3:ב: (14) Any amount — even less than a fingerbreadth (Acharonim):
3:ג: (15) At the opening of the mavo — see below siman 361:
3:ד: (16) Ten tefachim — spaced and not precise [Chiddushei R' Akiva Eiger]; and ten tefachim help even for a mavo twenty amot high:
3:ה: (17) And even if he tied, etc. — and it deals with when they did not inform that they placed it for the sake of lechi; if so certainly it will go away and not stand there all day, therefore we require specifically tying; and some are stringent even when they informed, lest he forget and go away from there:
4:א: (18) If there is some wall, etc. — although it was not made for the sake of lechi, we hold that a lechi standing by itself is also valid, as below in seif 11 see there:
4:ב: (19) A width of one tefach — see Biur Halacha:
5:א: (20) A lechi that if wind blows, etc. — and the same when making tzurat hapetach, for it is not better than a partition that cannot stand in an ordinary wind, which is not a partition [Tosafot Shabbos and Shach]; and even if the wind does not knock it to the ground but only shakes it, as written siman 362 seif 1:
5:ב: (21) Is not considered a lechi — it appears to me that if the lechi below does not shake, such as if fixed with a nail or tied well to the wall, and for this reason it does not shake until along a height of ten tefachim, and only above it shakes by wind because of its great height — it is valid, for from what remains above there is still lechi measure:
6:א: (22) It is required that it not be — some say the reason is because the air of this side and that side comes and nullifies it; and accordingly if the lechi were wider than three tefachim it is valid even if the lechi were distant three tefachim from the wall, for this is standing greater than the breach at its side, and in such a case we do not say the air comes and nullifies it; and some say that in every case the lechi must be within three tefachim of the wall, and one should be stringent:
6:ב: (23) The lechi — and when establishing tzurat hapetach for a mavo, the view of many poskim is that one need not be precise that it be within three tefachim of the wall, for tzurat hapetach is a complete partition; and some poskim hold there is no difference between tzurat hapetach and lechi for this matter, and in a time of need one may rely to be lenient. And if there are four tefachim between tzurat hapetach and the wall, the view of Chayei Adam is that one must place a lechi next to the wall; and for my part it requires further study also in this, as I clarified in Biur Halacha; and l'chatchila it is certainly proper to be concerned to be stringent even when distant three tefachim from the wall:
7:א: (24) A lechi — even fragments, etc. — meaning attached, provided it can stand in an ordinary wind [Levush]. And to exclude a korah, for we require specifically that it be strong enough to receive a brick, as below in seif 17:
7:ב: (25) Are valid for it — and the same for stones protruding from the wall and separated from one another less than three tefachim — they are an actual lechi, provided that between all of them there is a height of ten tefachim:
7:ג: (26) And therefore they make a lechi, etc. — for it is no worse than fragments of fragments, which are permitted for lechi; and the same for tzurat hapetach, for we require that lechayim be made on this side and that side; if he fears the wind will knock them down, it is permitted to make them by plaster smeared on the wall on this side and that side, and the reed above should be aligned upon them; and nevertheless we require that there be some substance at least like a thread; but appearance of plaster alone, or a mark in lime called krayid, or another color — does not help [Taz and Shach]:
7:ד: (27) That it not be erased more, etc. — meaning by dogs and pigs that are accustomed to rub against walls and erase from the walls the plaster smear near the ground; then it no longer helps, neither for lechi nor for tzurat hapetach:
7:ה: (28) More than three toward the ground — this wording is not precise, for even if only three were erased precisely, it is also nullified from being a lechi, as below in seif 10:
8:א: (29) A lechi that one made, etc. — in the Gemara it states that one may make a lechi from asherah wood, and it implies even l'chatchila. And one should not question: although for lechi, since it does not require measure, cut down its measure does not apply, as below — nevertheless it is forbidden in benefit; one may say that since the lechi is only for the sake of partition and one does not use anything in it itself, benefit from what one benefits through it for permitting carrying is not considered benefit [Beit Meir see there]:
8:ב: (30) Valid — the reason is that since a lechi does not require measure and any amount suffices, as above in seif 3, even from asherah wood it helps, although asherah wood stands for burning and is as if burned, and cut down its measure — nevertheless it does not require measure; and although here it still requires at least height measure of ten tefachim, since one can make it a very thin line of any amount, the Sages were not stringent about such a small measure; and they also answered in this that for lechi, even if the wood were burned to ash and kneaded with ash and glued to the wall, it is also considered a lechi, provided it is not removable by wind; therefore it is not disqualified because it stands for burning:
9:א: (31) And it is not visible to those standing outside — such as if he placed the lechi with its width along the length of the mavo and did not draw the end of its width slightly outward, but aligned its outer end with the thickness of the mavo wall, and it is like one who adds to the wall thickness and is not visible from outside as a lechi; but its inner end is visible to those standing inside, as in the source a diagram appears:
9:ב: (32) Opposite the hollow of the mavo — such as if he placed the entire lechi outside the mavo and its inner end stands at the wall thickness, but he did not place it flush with the edge of the wall thickness on the inner side of the mavo, for then it would not appear as a lechi but as adding to the wall even for those standing in reshus ha-rabbim; rather they distanced it from the corner of the inner wall thickness and placed it at the edge of the thickness of the rear side of the mavo, so that by this it is recognizable to those standing outside in reshus ha-rabbim opposite the hollow of the mavo that it is a lechi, as in the source a diagram appears:
9:ג: (33) For those standing inside — meaning for those standing inside the mavo the lechi is not visible, for it is not made on the inside:
10:א: (34) If he distanced it from the wall three — although it was already taught in seif 6, it repeated it to inform us that it is for invalidation:
10:ב: (35) Or if he raised it from the ground three — meaning even though the lechi has ten tefachim; and the reason is that it is not better than a partition removed three tefachim from the ground, which is invalid because it is a partition under which kids break through, which is not called a partition:
10:ג: (36) Valid — because of lavud, and it is as if this empty space were filled:
11:א: (37) That happened to be there by itself — such as if a projection came out from the mavo wall at its top in the measure of a length ten tefachim high, or it was placed there for some purpose, and even if they did not fix it — it itself has always been there — it is also valid, for lechi is because of partition, and a partition standing by itself is valid:
11:ב: (38) Such as if there was another lechi there, etc. — for it is as if he said on this I rely and not on this, and this one is as if rejected from the category of lechi [Or Zarua]:
11:ג: (39) As if they relied on it — meaning although they did not rely on it explicitly; however if they did not rely on it explicitly, such as if they did not carry on the past Shabbat through this lechi and there was no other lechi there, it does not help for the coming Shabbat until they rely on it explicitly from erev Shabbat:
12:א: (40) A lechi standing, etc. — the measure of his words is thus: for that which is written in seif 11 that a lechi standing by itself and they relied on it helps — specifically if the lechi does not protrude into the width of the mavo four amot; but if it protrudes and extends from the house wall into the width of the mavo four amot, then it leaves the category of lechi [because it has the qualifying measure of mavo length, which is four amot, as below in siman 366], and there it is a mavo wall upon it, and another lechi is required at the mavo opening to permit it — unless the mavo does not hold its width except eight amot, for then it is permitted without another lechi, for it is standing as breached and the mavo is considered closed on all sides, as likewise in siman 362 seif 9:
12:ב: (41) By itself — for if he placed it for the sake of lechi, even four amot wide, it is a lechi, as written in the gloss:
12:ג: (42) Four amot — for four amot is the measure of a mavo wall, and there is no recognition at all that it is a lechi; but up to four amot we can count it as a lechi, and this is when they relied on it from erev Shabbat, as likewise in seif 11:
12:ד: (43) Even four amot wide — and the same for more than this; and the reason is that because he increased at the mavo opening in its closing, it is no worse than an ordinary lechi [Rashi]:
13:א: (44) One who extends along its side, etc. — along the length of the mavo:
13:ב: (45) That the end of the lechi does not cover, etc. — rather it is shorter than it and extends beyond toward the rear of the mavo, as we illustrated above in seif 9 in Mishna Berurah:
13:ג: (46) Up to its inner end — meaning that through the lechi it is permitted to use the entire mavo up to the inner end of the lechi and no more; for although we hold in siman 365 seif 4 that between lechayim it is permitted to use, here it is different, for the other side is shorter than this, for there is no side opposite the lechi:
13:ד: (47) Four amot — it is judged as a mavo — for since it is four amot, which is generally the measure of mavo length, it leaves the category of lechi and is counted as a mavo wall; and likewise a mavo where one made along the length of the mavo inward many small lechayim arranged less than three tefachim from one another along four amot — the mavo is not permitted by this, for since they are less than three tefachim from one another, they are all considered as one lechi holding four amot in its width, and it leaves the category of lechi and is counted as a wall, and there is no lechi for this mavo. And nevertheless, if the first lechi standing at the end of the mavo does not stand flush with the end of the mavo but extends somewhat from the mavo inward, it is judged as lechi since it is visible from outside:
13:ה: (48) And it is forbidden to use — for this is forbidden even if it was placed for the sake of lechi, and it is not similar to what was stated above in seif 12, where they permit there when placed for lechi, for there he placed the projection across the width of the mavo and thereby its opening was closed, and therefore it is no worse than a lechi; unlike here, where he placed it along its length and it appears as adding further to the wall:
